I will not start from zero. I will start from what has worked on my land in Quzhou County and adjust for cost, labor, and water. I have 15 mu and only 2 people in the house, with some labor going off-farm, so I will keep the main area in the wheat-maize rotation because it is the most stable for me, easier to manage with machinery, and I have well irrigation. I will keep 10 mu in wheat-maize and leave 5 mu for cotton, so I do not put all my income in one crop. Since I studied more than most older farmers around me, I do look at input-output, not just habit. Wheat and maize are my grain backbone, so I will use improved or hybrid seed and keep fertilizer a little on the safe side, because losing yield costs more than wasting a small amount of fertilizer. On wheat, I will push nitrogen enough for a solid stand and good ears, but I will not let it run too lush. On maize, I will feed for a 650 kg per mu target, especially with my well water available if summer rain is uneven. Cotton takes more watching and more pesticide, but it spreads risk and cash flow, so I will still keep some area. I will use rotary tillage on wheat ground, simpler summer management on maize, and a deeper tillage pass for cotton ground. That way I can balance yield, labor, and cash through the whole year.
